clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter moving the family across the country in March 1952 and buying an apple orchard, within the year: June grew homesick and wrote daily to her sister, then kept to her bed for weeks that first winter; Walter spent long hours in the trees away from June; Glen began fights at his new school; Walter and his brother Harlan stopped speaking after a quarrel over their father's land money; Walter and June had rows over money for new trees. By September 1953, June joined the church choir and her letters thinned out, where the shifts settle.

clusters.name: Walter's orchard failure, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard failing in May 1968 when a late frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan, within the year: Walter began drinking heavily; he and Glen blamed each other for the loan; Glen and Marian took over the family's money and talks with the bank; Glen's son Carl's asthma attacks worsened that winter; Nora began wetting the bed again in April; Walter stopped drinking in October and took work pruning other men's trees, where the shifts settle. Nora's bedwetting and her father's symptoms shifted together in these months.

clusters.name: Glen's job loss at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen losing his job when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975, within the year: Glen sat out of work in the truck for hours; he and Marian had loud fights at night over money; Marian took a second job cleaning offices at night; Nora stopped eating properly and lost weight that summer; Nora kept to her room and said little to her mother; Walter began drinking again after six years; Nora's eating returned and she made the track team by June 1976, where the shifts settle.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into Nora and Sam's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma, Sam's widowed mother, selling her farm and moving into Nora and Sam's house in January 1990, within the year: Nora and Wilma clashed over the children's bedtimes and meals; Sam worked late and kept out of the kitchen rows; Sam took his mother's side; Owen had tantrums at preschool; Wilma took over Lily's care; Nora's eczema flared on both hands; Nora and Sam had rows most nights. By June 1991, Wilma took a flat in town, and Nora's eczema cleared over the summer, where the shifts settle.
